rationale: The agent identified the user via name and ZIP and retrieved user and order details, which is acceptable authentication given the provided tools. However, it then executed order-changing writes without first confirming with the user: it modified the delivery address, swapped a watch item, and changed the air purifier variant, and even charged the credit card for the price difference, all without explicit user confirmation. Policy requires confirmation before any order-changing action. Additionally, the user indicated the purifier was already received; the agent used a pending-order modification tool rather than verifying delivery status and initiating an exchange/return flow or escalating if needed. Finally, the agent’s final summary was truncated and did not clearly confirm the color preference or exactly which watch was changed, leaving key details unverified. These issues violate the pass criteria.
